T1: Individual consumers will adopt a differentiated hearing-protection proposition if it addresses a specific use case (e.g., musicians) and offers a clear functional advantage (e.g., preserves sound quality) that current options lack. Who benefits: Consumers seeking optimal hearing protection for a specific activity (e.g., musicians who need to hear performances without compromising safety).. Why behaviour changes: Current hearing protection (e.g., generic earplugs) reduces sound quality, limiting enjoyment and utility. A product that preserves sound while providing adequate protection will be perceived as a necessary investment.. How value is captured: Hellberg can charge a premium price for the differentiated proposition and sell directly to consumers via e-commerce or specialty retailers, capturing higher margins than generic earplugs.. Assumptions: Consumers are willing to pay a premium for sound-preserving hearing protection.; There is sufficient awareness of Hellberg among target consumers to find and purchase the product.; The functional advantage is measurable and communicated effectively.. Predictions: In a test offering a sound-preserving version of Hellberg’s existing earplugs to musicians, purchase intent will be at least 15% higher than for a generic version.; Willingness to pay will be at least 20% higher for the sound-preserving model compared to a standard model..

T2: Individual consumers will adopt a differentiated hearing-protection proposition if it is positioned as a fashion or lifestyle accessory that signals status and personal expression, especially among younger demographics who value aesthetics and brand. Who benefits: Consumers seeking a visible, stylish hearing protection solution that aligns with personal style and social media identity.. Why behaviour changes: Current hearing protection is often perceived as utilitarian and uncomfortable, leading consumers to avoid it. A product that combines protection with fashion appeal reduces perceived awkwardness and becomes a desirable accessory.. How value is captured: Hellberg can partner with fashion brands, launch limited-edition designs, and sell through lifestyle retailers, capturing higher margins through premium pricing and brand extension.. Assumptions: Young consumers are willing to pay a premium for stylish hearing protection.; Fashion-forward retailers will stock a differentiated proposition.; The fashion aspect does not compromise safety performance.. Predictions: In a test offering a fashion-designed version of Hellberg’s earplugs to a sample of 20‑30‑year‑olds, purchase intent will be at least 10% higher than for a standard model.; Willingness to pay for the fashion version will be at least 15% higher than for a standard model..

Predictions: T1: Health-conscious segment will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP at $120 than status-conscious segment.; T2: Status-conscious segment will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP at $180 than health-conscious segment.. If status-conscious segment purchase intent at $180 exceeds health-conscious segment by at least 10 percentage points AND average WTP for status segment is at least $180, then T2 is supported. If neither condition is met, both theories remain. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.
